headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Hiring an Interior Remodeling Contractor
articleBody:
Starting an interior renovation without careful groundwork can turn an exciting home update into a stressful, expensive ordeal. Homeowners often run into avoidable headaches by skipping essential planning steps.

Common Mistakes to Avoid:
1. Starting work before permits are issued. Always verify local building department requirements, because covering up uninspected rough plumbing or electrical work can force expensive demolition later.
2. Relying on vague scopes of work. Make sure every contract itemizes specific materials, brand finishes, cleanup duties, and waste removal details.
3. Overlooking change-order procedures. Unexpected issues happen behind old walls; establish a clear, written process for handling cost or schedule changes before construction begins.
4. Skipping payment milestones. Never pay entirely upfront; tie your payments to verified project milestones and passed inspections.
5. Choosing a contractor on price alone. A low bid often hides missing permit fees, cheaper materials, or excluded trades that appear later as surprise expenses.
